stories.title: Shooting in Krakow's Main Market Square Leaves Six Dead and Over a Dozen Injured
stories.summary: A shooting incident in the Main Market Square of Krakow, Poland, resulted in six fatalities and at least 15 injuries. The gunman, a Polish citizen, reportedly opened fire from his car before being shot and wounded by police. Authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding this tragic event, which is notable as mass shootings are rare in Poland.

stories.title: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña Impeached and Arrested Amid Banking Crisis
stories.summary: Santiago Peña has been impeached and placed under house arrest following a banking crisis that left nearly three million customers unable to access their funds. The Senate voted unanimously for his removal over allegations related to the collapse of Ueno Bank. Pedro Alliana has been sworn in as the new president, pledging to compensate those affected by the crisis.

stories.summary: President Donald Trump has appointed Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. Miller, known for his hardline immigration policies, is expected to reinforce Trump's agenda following disappointing midterm election results. His promotion signals a commitment to the administration's controversial domestic policies.

stories.title: Kenyan Cult Leader Sentenced to 200 Years for Murdering 191 People
stories.summary: Paul Mackenzie, the leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect, has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult. The court found that he incited his followers to starve themselves and their families in a bid to 'meet Jesus.' Mackenzie and 28 accomplices were convicted for their roles in this tragic incident.

stories.title: Thomas Markle Arrested on Child Sexual Abuse Material Charges
stories.summary: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan Markle, has been arrested in Florida on charges of possessing child sexual abuse materials. The Justice Department reported that the allegations include having sexually explicit photographs involving minors. Following his arrest, Markle appeared in court and is currently under house arrest after the FBI conducted searches of storage units he rented in the Los Angeles area.

stories.title: ANC Faces Significant Decline in South African Local Elections
stories.summary: The African National Congress (ANC) is projected to receive less than a third of the vote in South Africa's local elections, marking a significant decline from previous years. With over 80% of ballots counted, the ANC is on track for its worst-ever election performance, estimated at around 32%. This decline is attributed to widespread voter dissatisfaction over issues such as water outages and power cuts, leading to potential coalition challenges in major cities like Johannesburg and Tshwane.

stories.title: Cornell Faculty Votes No Confidence in Leadership Over Handling of Sexual Assault Case

This decision comes in response to criticism regarding the administration's handling of a sexual assault case involving a former student who alleged she was drugged and raped at a fraternity house in October 2024. Faculty members hope this vote will prompt the university's trustees to address perceived institutional failures.

stories.title: Jay Rockefeller, Former Governor and Senator, Passes Away at 89

He served as the governor of West Virginia and was a longtime U.S. senator, known for his advocacy on healthcare, education, and working families' needs. Rockefeller was born into a prominent family and forged a significant political career.

The region has seen intense clashes recently, contributing to a worsening humanitarian crisis.
